However, the test failure indicates that this is not the case. Following the execution path, we find that in the `unified_strdate` method (in package `youtube_dl.utils`), the function is not successfully converting the input date string `'1968-12-10'`. The reason lies in the fact that the method uses a list of format expressions to attempt to match and parse the input date string using various formats. When it encounters an input date string, it tries each expression sequentially until one succeeds. In this case, although there is no explicit failure (i.e., `ValueError`) when trying to parse `'1968-12-10'` with any of the expressions, it turns out that none of them match correctly. The next attempt to convert the date string into a unified format using `email.utils.parsedate_tz` also fails silently because it returns `None`. As a result, the method incorrectly returns `None` instead of the expected formatted string. This leads to the error demonstrated by the test.
